WWDC 2026 Recap: Apple Is Building Faster, Smarter, and More Personal Operating Systems

Written by Seojin Lee, Apple Developer Academy Cohort 2026

WWDC 2026 gave us a clear look at where Apple wants to take its ecosystem next.

As a member of the Apple Developer Academy Cohort 2026, I found WWDC 2026 especially meaningful because it showed how Apple is shaping the future of software, AI, and spatial computing across its ecosystem.

This year’s announcements were not only about visual changes or new interface details. Instead, Apple seemed to focus on a deeper direction: making its operating systems faster, more intelligent, more personal, and more closely connected to users’ everyday lives.

From macOS performance improvements to Photos app speed, from deeper search indexing to Health features, and from AirPods personalization to Vision Pro experiences, WWDC 2026 showed that Apple is trying to make its devices understand users more naturally.

One of the biggest themes this year was Apple’s next-generation AI strategy. Apple worked together with Gemini to build a next-generation foundation model experience, connecting on-device models, server-side models, and Spotlight into a more intelligent system-level layer.

The most interesting part was that many of the updates were not just “new features.” They were improvements to the basic layers of the user experience: how quickly the system responds, how well it understands personal data, how health information is managed, and how spatial computing can make familiar apps feel new again.

In this post, I want to summarize the key updates that stood out to me and explain what they suggest about Apple’s direction.

1. macOS 27 Golden Gate: Focusing on System Fundamentals

One of the major announcements was macOS 27 Golden Gate.

While the name and design updates are important, what stood out to me most was Apple’s focus on improving the fundamentals of the operating system. A good OS is not only about how it looks. It is also about how efficiently it manages resources, how smoothly apps run, and how naturally users can move between different tasks.

One of the most interesting technical updates was the improvement to the CPU scheduler.

The CPU scheduler is not something most users directly think about. It does not appear as a button or a visible feature in the interface. However, it has a huge impact on how fast and responsive the system feels.

When a user runs multiple apps at the same time, the operating system needs to decide which tasks should receive more processing power. For example, if someone is editing a video, running a development environment, browsing the web, and using AI-powered tools at the same time, the system needs to manage those workloads efficiently.

This is where the CPU scheduler becomes important.

By improving CPU scheduling, Apple can make macOS feel smoother in real-world usage. Apps may launch faster, background tasks may interfere less with active work, and heavy workflows may feel more stable.

This also fits well with Apple’s broader strategy around Apple Silicon. Since Apple controls both the hardware and software, it can optimize performance at a deeper level than companies that only control one side of the experience.

In other words, macOS 27 Golden Gate is not just about a new name or a new design. It shows Apple’s continued focus on making the Mac faster, more efficient, and more reliable for demanding users.

2. Siri AI: Apple Intelligence and Foundation Models: Built Together With Gemini

Another major direction from WWDC 2026 was Apple’s next-generation AI strategy.

This year, Apple worked together with Gemini to build a next-generation foundation model experience. What made this especially interesting was that Apple did not present AI as a separate chatbot or standalone app. Instead, it showed AI as a system-level layer connected directly to the operating system.

The most important point was the connection between on-device models, server-side models, and Spotlight.

On-device AI allows the system to process personal information quickly and privately. This matters because Apple devices contain deeply personal context, such as photos, messages, calendars, app activity, health data, and documents. By handling many tasks on the device, Apple can provide faster and more private intelligence.

At the same time, some tasks require more powerful models than what a device can handle alone. For these cases, Apple can connect to server-side models. This hybrid approach makes the AI experience more flexible: simple and personal tasks can happen on-device, while more complex reasoning or generation tasks can use larger models on the server.

The most exciting part is how this connects to Spotlight.

Spotlight is no longer just a search bar. By connecting Apple’s on-device intelligence, server models, and Gemini-powered foundation models, Spotlight can become a much smarter interface for finding information and taking action across the device.

Instead of only searching for app names or file names, users may be able to search based on context, memory, and intent.

For example:

  • “Find the photo from my trip where I was near the bridge.”
  • “Show me the document I edited after the meeting.”
  • “Open the note related to my health appointment.”
  • “Summarize the files connected to this project.”

This kind of experience requires more than keyword search. It needs a system that understands personal context, app data, user intent, and privacy boundaries.

That is why the combination of Gemini, on-device AI, server-side models, and Spotlight feels so important.

It suggests that Apple is trying to make AI part of the entire OS experience. The future of Apple Intelligence may not be about opening a separate AI app. Instead, intelligence will quietly live inside the system, helping users search, understand, organize, and act more naturally.

3. Photos App: 5x Faster Loading and Stronger Recognition

The Photos app also received meaningful improvements.

One of the most noticeable updates was that photo loading is now up to five times faster. This may sound like a simple performance improvement, but it actually matters a lot in everyday use.

Today, people take thousands of photos and videos. The Photos app is no longer just a place to store images. It has become a personal visual database. It helps users remember people, places, events, pets, trips, and important moments.

Because of this, speed is very important.

If the Photos app is slow, users feel friction every time they try to find a memory. But if photos load instantly and search works smoothly, the app becomes much more useful.

Another important improvement is stronger recognition. Apple appears to be expanding the system’s ability to understand people, scenes, and shared content more intelligently.

This is especially interesting for shared albums.

Shared albums are not just personal storage spaces. They are often used by families, friends, classmates, teams, and communities. If Apple can improve recognition inside shared albums, the Photos app becomes better at organizing memories across relationships, not only within one individual’s personal library.

This shows that Apple is thinking about photos not only as media files, but as meaningful personal and social data.

The Photos app is becoming faster, smarter, and more context-aware.

4. iOS 27 Support From iPhone 11: The Value of Long-Term Device Support

Another important point is that iOS 27 will be available starting from iPhone 11.

This is significant because long-term software support is one of Apple’s biggest strengths. Many users do not upgrade their iPhone every year. Some people use the same device for four, five, or even more years.

When an older device still receives the latest iOS update, users can continue to access new software features, security improvements, design updates, and system-level optimizations.

This is not only good for users. It also strengthens the entire Apple ecosystem.

If more devices can run the latest version of iOS, developers can build apps for a more unified platform. They do not have to worry as much about supporting too many outdated versions. This helps create a more consistent experience across the ecosystem.

From the user’s perspective, iOS 27 support from iPhone 11 means that the value of an iPhone lasts longer.

It also sends a clear message: the newest software experience should not be limited only to the newest hardware.

Of course, some advanced features may still depend on newer chips or specific hardware capabilities. But broad OS support itself is meaningful because it keeps older devices useful, secure, and connected to Apple’s latest direction.

5. Search: Moving Toward Deeper App Indexing

Search was another area that stood out to me.

In the past, system search was mostly about finding app names, contacts, documents, or simple information. However, Apple seems to be moving toward a deeper form of search that can index more information from installed apps.

This means search may become more connected to the actual content and actions inside apps.

For example, users often remember the information they need, but not where it is stored. They might remember a photo, a message, a note, a document, or a detail inside an app, but they may not remember the exact location.

A stronger search system can reduce that friction.

Instead of asking, “Which app did I use?” or “Where did I save that?”, users can simply search for what they remember. The operating system can then help connect them to the right place.

This changes the meaning of system search.

Search is no longer just a tool for finding files. It can become a personal interface that connects information, context, and actions across the device.

This is also closely related to Apple’s broader intelligence strategy. If the system can understand more about installed apps and user context while preserving privacy, the device becomes much more useful without requiring the user to manually organize everything.

In the long term, search may become one of the most important interfaces in the OS.

6. Health App: Expanding Into Menopause Support

The Health app also received an important update with support for menopause-related health tracking.

This stood out to me because it shows Apple’s Health strategy becoming more life-stage focused.

Apple Health already handles many types of personal health data, including heart rate, sleep, activity, menstrual cycle tracking, and other wellness-related information. By expanding into menopause support, Apple is moving beyond general fitness and wellness into more specific long-term health needs.

Menopause is a health experience that can vary greatly from person to person. It can involve physical, emotional, and lifestyle-related changes over a long period of time.

Because of that, tracking and understanding patterns can be valuable.

If designed carefully, menopause-related features could help users observe changes in symptoms, sleep, activity, mood, and other health signals. It could also make it easier for users to discuss their patterns with healthcare professionals.

This update also reflects a broader shift in consumer health technology.

Health features are becoming more personal, more continuous, and more connected to different stages of life. Instead of only tracking steps or workouts, devices are starting to support more complex and long-term health experiences.

For Apple, this is a meaningful direction.

It suggests that the Health app is becoming a personal health platform, not just a fitness companion.

7. AirPods Custom EQ: A More Personalized Listening Experience

AirPods also gained a custom EQ feature.

At first, this may sound like a small audio feature. But I think it reflects a larger trend: Apple is making audio more personal.

Everyone hears sound differently. People also have different preferences depending on music genre, environment, hearing ability, and content type. Some users may prefer stronger bass, while others may want clearer vocals or softer high frequencies.

A custom EQ allows users to adjust the listening experience more closely to their own preferences.

This is important because AirPods are no longer used only for music. People use them for phone calls, video meetings, online classes, movies, podcasts, language learning, accessibility features, and even health-related audio experiences.

As AirPods become more deeply integrated into everyday life, personalization becomes more important.

This also connects to accessibility. A more customizable audio experience can help users who need different sound profiles. It can make voices easier to hear, reduce discomfort, or improve clarity in specific situations.

AirPods are gradually becoming more than wireless earphones.

They are becoming personal audio devices that adapt to the user.

8. Vision Pro: Expanding Panoramic Photos and Maps

The Vision Pro-related updates were also impressive.

One of the interesting features was the ability to view panoramic photos more immersively on Vision Pro.

Panoramic photos have existed for a long time, but they have usually been experienced on flat screens. On an iPhone, users swipe left and right to view the full image. It is useful, but it does not fully capture the feeling of being in the place where the photo was taken.

Vision Pro changes this experience.

When panoramic photos are viewed in a spatial environment, they can feel more like scenes surrounding the user. A simple photo becomes more immersive and emotional.

This is a good example of how Vision Pro can make familiar content feel new again.

Another important update was related to Maps.

The Maps app became more enhanced with Vision Intelligence. Rather than simply showing directions or location pins, Maps can become a more visual and intelligent way to understand places.

With Vision Intelligence, Maps can provide a richer and more intuitive experience. It can help users understand surrounding environments, place-based information, and spatial context more naturally.

This matters because maps are not only about navigation. They are about understanding space.

When visual intelligence is added to maps, the experience can become more useful for travel, local discovery, urban exploration, and accessibility.

For Vision Pro, this is especially meaningful. Spatial computing needs apps that can connect digital information with physical space. Maps is one of the best examples of that.

By combining Vision Pro, panoramic photos, and enhanced Maps experiences, Apple is showing how everyday apps can evolve in the era of spatial computing.

9. Vision Pro and Health: Spatial Computing Meets Personal Wellness

Another interesting direction is the connection between Vision Pro and health.

Health data is usually shown through numbers, charts, and dashboards. While this is useful, it can sometimes feel abstract. Users may see their heart rate, sleep score, or activity trends, but it may be difficult to understand what those numbers mean in a more intuitive way.

Vision Pro could change how health data is experienced.

In a spatial environment, health information could become more visual, interactive, and easier to understand. For example, users might see body-related information, movement feedback, posture guidance, or recovery progress in a more immersive format.

This could be especially useful in areas like rehabilitation, physical therapy, sports training, and wellness coaching.

Of course, this area still requires careful design, scientific validation, and privacy protection. Health data is sensitive, and spatial health experiences should be based on trustworthy research.

However, the potential is clear.

Vision Pro may not only be a device for entertainment or productivity. It could also become a platform for new kinds of health and wellness experiences.

10. Children and Families: Research-Based Design Matters

Another theme that stood out was Apple’s attention to children and families.

What I found meaningful was that Apple did not seem to treat child-related features only as simple parental controls. Instead, the message felt more thoughtful: every child’s experience matters.

Technology plays a major role in children’s daily lives. Devices are used for learning, communication, entertainment, creativity, and social interaction. Because of this, designing technology for children requires more responsibility.

It is not enough to simply limit screen time.

Companies need to think about how children use technology, what kind of content they are exposed to, how families can guide them, and how digital experiences affect their well-being.

Apple’s emphasis on expert research and youth-focused guidance is important here. Features for children and teenagers should not be based only on business goals or assumptions. They should be informed by research, experts, and real-world family needs.

This shows a more responsible direction.

As digital devices become more personal and more intelligent, child safety and family-centered design will become even more important.

11. The Bigger Picture: Apple Is Making the OS More Context-Aware

Overall, WWDC 2026 showed that Apple is not simply adding more features.

Apple is making its operating systems more context-aware.

The Photos app is not just storing images. It is understanding memories.

Search is not just finding files. It is connecting information across apps.

Spotlight is not just a search tool. It is becoming a smarter interface powered by on-device intelligence, server-side models, and Gemini-supported foundation models.

Health is not just tracking activity. It is supporting different stages of life.

AirPods are not just playing sound. They are adapting to personal listening needs.

Vision Pro is not just showing digital windows. It is transforming how users experience photos, maps, and potentially health information.

This is the larger direction I saw from WWDC 2026.

Apple is building an ecosystem where devices understand users more naturally, respond faster, and support more personal experiences.

The most important updates may not always be the most visually dramatic ones. Sometimes, the most meaningful changes happen at the system level: faster loading, better scheduling, stronger indexing, improved recognition, and more personalized experiences.

That is why WWDC 2026 felt less like a simple software update and more like a step toward a more intelligent and personal computing environment.

Final Thoughts

For me, WWDC 2026 was interesting because it showed Apple’s long-term strategy very clearly.

The future of Apple’s OS is not only about beautiful design. It is about building systems that are faster, smarter, more personal, and more connected to real human needs.

macOS 27 Golden Gate focuses on performance and system fundamentals.

Apple Intelligence is becoming more powerful through Gemini-supported foundation models, on-device processing, server-side models, and Spotlight integration.

Photos becomes faster and better at understanding shared memories.

iOS 27 support from iPhone 11 shows the value of long-term device support.

Search is moving toward deeper indexing and a more assistant-like experience.

Health is expanding into life-stage support.

AirPods are becoming more personalized.

Vision Pro is showing how spatial computing can transform familiar apps like Photos and Maps.

And Apple’s family-related features suggest that research-based design will become increasingly important.

In short, WWDC 2026 showed that Apple is not just redesigning its operating systems.

Apple is trying to make them understand people better.

item.title: 배치 성능 최적화 (+병렬화)
item.content:encoded:
실행계획 — 배치 성능 최적화

복잡도와 의존관계 고려해서 정리. 측정 환경: dev 에선 효과 안 보임 — 운영 5만 또는 시드 부풀려서 측정해야 함.

사전 작업 — 측정 기반 마련 (필수, 코드 변경 X)

이게 먼저 없으면 1~5 의 효과를 비교할 수 없음.

┌─────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 항목 │ 작업 │ ├─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ 배치 phase 별 타이밍 │ NightlyMatchBatch.run 에 phase 별 System.nanoTime() 마커 추가 — [viewer cache 로드 / score 계산 / replaceDailyFeed] 각각 ms 누계 + viewer 100명마다 │ │ 로그 │ mid-progress 로그 │ ├─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ viewer 별 평균 ms │ process(me, cfg, today, cache) 전체 ms / viewer count │ ├─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ baseline │ 현재 상태 (f4779a2 + LIMIT 제거) 에서 1회 측정해 숫자 박제 │ └─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

→ 1~5 마다 baseline 대비 차이 측정.

Step 3 — 병렬화 (가장 효과 큼)

가설: viewer 처리는 100% 독립 → CPU 1코어 × DB 1 conn 로만 도는 게 병목. N thread 면 N배.

3-1. ThreadPoolExecutor 설정

application.yml — match-batch 전용 pool

match-batch: threads: 8 # CPU 코어 - 2 정도 (운영 서버 스펙 확인 필요) queue: 1000

MatchBatchExecutorConfig 신설 — @Bean("matchBatchExecutor") ThreadPoolTaskExecutor. corePoolSize/maxPoolSize/queueCapacity + setThreadNamePrefix("match-batch-").

3-2. NightlyMatchBatch.run — 병렬 분기

List viewers = userMgmt.findEligibleViewers(cfg); Map<Long, UserContext> cache = userMgmt.loadAllActiveContextsAsMap(cfg);

List<CompletableFuture> futures = viewers.stream() .map(me -> CompletableFuture.runAsync( () -> processSafely(me, cfg, today, cache), // try/catch 안에서 1 viewer 처리 matchBatchExecutor)) .toList(); CompletableFuture.allOf(futures.toArray(new CompletableFuture[0])).join();

processSafely 는 기존 MyFeedRecomputer.process 호출 + viewer 단위 try/catch (한 명 실패가 다른 viewer 영향 X).

3-3. DB connection pool 키우기

spring.datasource.hikari: maximum-pool-size: 16 # 8 thread + 여유 (현재 기본값 10 → 16) minimum-idle: 8

→ thread 가 pool 보다 많으면 conn 대기로 병렬화 무의미.

3-4. 위험 + 검증

┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 위험 │ 대응 │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ @Transactional propagation 충돌 — process 가 readOnly + 안에서 │ 각 viewer 가 독립 thread + 독립 conn 이라 transaction 도 독립. 검증 필요 │ │ write (replaceDailyFeed) │ │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ ShedLock (@SchedulerLock) 은 메인 thread 기준 — 병렬 thread 와 │ 그대로 OK │ │ 무관 │ │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ EntityManager thread-safety │ @PersistenceContext 기본은 thread-bound. 병렬 호출 시 각 thread 가 새 EntityManager 받아야 함 — @Transactional 이 │ │ │ thread 단위로 EntityManager 발급하므로 OK │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Deadlock — 같은 row 동시 update │ viewer 별 row 가 disjoint (viewer_id 기준) 라 충돌 없음 │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ KeywordFreqService 등 공유 상태 │ read-only 이면 OK. 캐시 갱신은 배치 시작 전 1회만 │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ log MDC / RequestContext │ 배치 thread 는 request 컨텍스트 없음 — 영향 X │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

검증: 8 thread 로 1회 → baseline 대비 5~7배 빨라져야 정상. 안 되면 다른 병목 (DB lock).

예상 효과: 6h → ~50min

Step 2 — Hibernate batch insert

가설: replaceDailyFeed 가 viewer 1명당 ~45 row INSERT. row 마다 별도 round-trip이면 5만 × 45 = 225만 round-trip.

2-1. yml 설정

spring.jpa.properties.hibernate: jdbc.batch_size: 50 order_inserts: true order_updates: true batch_versioned_data: true

2-2. JDBC URL — rewriteBatchedStatements=true

jdbc:mariadb://.../...?rewriteBatchedStatements=true&...

→ MariaDB connector 가 batch 50 row 를 하나의 multi-value INSERT 로 재작성. 이게 없으면 batch_size 설정해도 효과 1/10.

2-3. replaceDailyFeed 코드 확인

  • em.persist() + flush() 패턴이어야 batch. native INSERT ... VALUES (?,?) 를 loop 로 돌리면 batch 안 됨

  • 현재 패턴이 native query loop 이면 → INSERT INTO match_daily_feed (...) VALUES (...), (...), (...) ... multi-value 로 통째로 바꾸는 게 빠름 (재작성 의존 안 함)

    2-4. 위험

    ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 위험 │ 대응 │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ INSERT IGNORE (RecentNewbieBatch) 는 batch 와 다른 │ 그건 그대로 (한 row 씩) │ │ 패턴 │ │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ ID 가 IDENTITY 면 batch insert 비활성화 │ match_daily_feed PK 가 AUTO_INCREMENT 면 영향 — TABLE/SEQUENCE 또는 application-side ID 검토. 단 multi-value INSERT 는 IDENTITY │ │ │ 와 무관하게 작동 │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    예상 효과: 50min → ~30min (병렬화 위에서)

Step 4 — score cache (가장 큰 작업, 효과 의심)

§10.20-A 에서 완전 폐기한 match_score_cache 를 다른 목적으로 재도입.

4-1. 가설 검증 먼저

MatchCalculator.score 가 페어당 실제 얼마 걸리는지 측정 — 메모리 산술이면 100us 수준이고, 5만 × 500 = 2500만 페어 × 100us = 2500초 (42분). 점수 계산이 진짜 병목인지 확인해야 함.

병목이면 → 4번 진행. 아니면 (DB I/O가 진짜 병목) → Step 4 skip, Step 5 로 직행.

4-2. 캐시 설계 — match_score_cache_v2

CREATE TABLE match_score_cache ( viewer_id BIGINT NOT NULL, target_id BIGINT NOT NULL, keyword_score DOUBLE, ideal_score DOUBLE, lifestyle_score DOUBLE, location_score DOUBLE, computed_at DATETIME NOT NULL, viewer_changed_at DATETIME NOT NULL, -- 캐시 hit 판단용 target_changed_at DATETIME NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (viewer_id, target_id), INDEX (computed_at) );

4-3. cache hit 판단

// 페어 계산 전: if (cache.viewerChangedAt >= me.profileUpdatedAt && cache.targetChangedAt >= other.profileUpdatedAt) { return cache.toPairScore(); // hit — 계산 skip } PairScore ps = calculator.score(me, other, cfg); cache.upsert(me.id, other.id, ps, me.profileUpdatedAt, other.profileUpdatedAt);

→ user.last_profile_change_at (또는 update_time) 필요. 기존 컬럼 활용 가능한지 확인.

4-4. 위험 + 부담

┌─────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┐ │ 위험 │ 대응 │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┤ │ tags_json freeze 정책과 충돌 (§10.20-A) │ 받은 좋아요 단건 표시용 tags_json 은 그대로 — 캐시는 배치 score 계산 가속용으로만 │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┤ │ 캐시 row 5만 × 500 = 2500만 row │ INDEX (computed_at) 로 오래된 거 cleanup. 30일 retention │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┤ │ 캐시 miss 첫 배치는 의미 X │ 첫 배치 후 다음 batch 부터 효과 │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┤ │ 캐시 자체 I/O (read + write) 가 새 비용 │ hit ratio 가 충분히 높아야 의미 — 프로필 변경 빈도 낮으면 high hit │ └─────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┘

작업량: 큼. 테이블 + 엔티티 + Repository + Service + hit/miss 로직 + cleanup cron. ~1일.

예상 효과: 점수 계산이 진짜 병목일 때만 의미. 측정 후 결정 권장.

Step 1 — DEBUG → INFO 로그

1-1. yml

logging.level: com.nokcha.efbe.domain.match: INFO com.nokcha.efbe.infra.scheduler.match: INFO

1-2. 코드 — log.debug(...) 가 hot path 에 있어도 무방하지만, 인자 계산 비용 큰 debug 는 가드:

if (log.isDebugEnabled()) log.debug("score me={} other={} ps={}", ...);

특히 tagsJson 직렬화 같은 무거운 debug 인자.

예상 효과: 작음 (5~10%) 하지만 공짜.

Step 5 — "변화 없으면 DELETE+INSERT skip"

5-1. 가설

replaceDailyFeed 는 매일 viewer 1명당 45 row 통째 교체. 어제 top-50 과 오늘 top-50 set 이 같으면 (또는 95% 같으면) DB write 자체 skip.

5-2. 구현

List todayTargetSet = scored.stream().sorted(...).limit(50).map(...).toList(); List yesterdayTargetSet = dailyFeedRepo.findTargetIdsByViewerId(me.id()); if (todayTargetSet.equals(yesterdayTargetSet)) { log.debug("[Skip] viewer={} feed unchanged", me.id()); return; // DB write 안 함 } dailyFeedRepo.replaceDailyFeed(me.id(), today, rows);

5-3. 위험

  • tags_json / sort_key 가 day-by-day 로 바뀔 수도 있음 (예: KeywordFreqService 의 빈도 변화) — set 비교만으로 안 됨, row 자체 hash 가 필요할 수도

  • match_daily_feed.created_at 이 안 갱신되면 "어제 feed 이지만 오늘 row 처럼 보임" — 의미 충돌. read-time 쿼리가 feed_date = CURDATE() 보면 OK

  • 부분 변경 (50 중 5명만 바뀜) → set 비교 X, 그땐 통째 교체가 단순
